outcome: A single-author preprint (Amir Jafari, New Uzbekistan University) posted August 24, 2026 (revised September 16, 2026) proves the stronger 'online' form of the List Edge-Coloring Conjecture for two new infinite families of complete graphs, K_{p-1} and K_{2p} for odd primes p, extending the set of complete graphs for which the conjecture is known to hold. The general conjecture remains open, and this result has not yet been digested by experts (no citations, no journal acceptance, single recent preprint).
summary: The triage record flagged an August 2026 arXiv preprint by Amir Jafari (arXiv:2608.22895, v1 2026-08-24, v2 2026-09-16) proving the stronger online version of the List Edge-Coloring Conjecture (equivalent to the List Coloring Conjecture as worded on Wikipedia: for every graph, list chromatic index equals chromatic index) for two new infinite families of complete graphs: K_{p-1} and K_{2p} for odd primes p. I opened and read the abstract and HTML full text. The paper builds on prior known cases (bipartite multigraphs via Galvin 1995; odd-order complete graphs via Häggkvist-Janssen; order p+1 for odd prime p via Schauz 2014; K_10 via Rabern's enumeration) and explicitly states 'the unresolved complete graphs therefore have even order,' confirming this is a partial result narrowing (but not closing) the open cases among complete graphs, not a resolution of the general conjecture. I found no mention of AI systems, LLMs, or automated proof search anywhere in the paper's introduction, methods, or acknowledgements — the author's affiliation is listed but there is no separate acknowledgements section crediting any tool. I searched broadly for any other 2024-2026 progress on this conjecture (disproofs, counterexamples, AI involvement) and found none: the Wikipedia article on 'List of mathematical discoveries by artificial intelligence' has no entry for this conjecture, the dynamic survey on list-coloring (arXiv:2606.31702) does not mention it, and general web searches for AI-related work on list edge coloring turned up nothing relevant (results about the unrelated 'List Square Coloring Conjecture' and general LLM graph-coloring benchmarks, not this conjecture). The paper is a single-author preprint with no citations yet and no journal acceptance, so it counts as a settled case (partial) rather than resolved/claimed of the whole conjecture — since the sub-result itself (specific new infinite families of complete graphs) is a concrete, checkable mathematical proof rather than a sweeping claim awaiting verification, and does not require the same 'has an expert dug into it' bar that a full resolution claim would need to be trusted as a genuine advance on that scope. I classify resolution_direction as 'confirmed' because the settled cases (K_{p-1}, K_{2p}) satisfy the conjecture as conjectured, not against it.
competing_reading: One could argue this preprint, being unreviewed and from a single author with no other citations, should be treated more cautiously (effectively 'claimed' pending verification) rather than 'partial,' since 'partial' as defined presumes the settled case is solid. I lean toward 'partial' because the result is a self-contained, checkable finite/algebraic argument about specific graph families (not a sweeping general claim), and nothing in my search suggested any error or dispute; but a future reviewer who finds a flaw in the matching-sum argument would need to downgrade this.
what_would_settle_it: An expert digestion, citation, or journal acceptance of arXiv:2608.22895 confirming the proof is correct; alternatively, a rebuttal or erratum showing an error in the argument.
